sentences.text:
This petition has been filed by the petitioner under Article 226 of the Constitution of India challenging the order dated 22.8.2016 (Annexure P/1) passed by respondent No.1 whereby the review application made by the petitioner for cancellation of his resignation which was accepted by the District Education Officer vide order dated 11.6.2007, has been rejected.
Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:9250 Surendra Kumar Upadhyay vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190803494/
1 02.

entities.text: CGHC:9250 Surendra Kumar Upadhyay vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case, as mentioned in the writ petition, are that the petitioner was initially appointed as Upper Division Teacher vide order dated 4.4.1987.

However, due to some family disputes as the petitioner's wife filed a complaint under Section 498A & 323 of IPC against him and also sought maintenance from him, he made an application for his resignation on 8.12.2006 and later on again on 3.1.2007 he made application for resignation vide Annexure P/2.

Thereafter,
respondent No.3 vide letter dated 19.1.2007 (Annexure P/3) directed the petitioner to submit one month salary through Challan, No Objection Certificate and recommendation from the Block Education Officer.

However, on 7.5.2007 the petitioner submitted an application before the District Education Officer, Janjgir-Champa (Annexure P/4) wherein he sought information regarding the required length of service for entitlement of voluntary retirement, pension; his total leaves; the rule prescribing deposit of one month salary for seeking VRS or resignation etc.

Respondent No.3 overlooking the said application of the petitioner on 7.6.2007 through Block Education Officer deposited one month salary of the petitioner through challan and vide order dated 11.6.2007 (Annexure P/6) accepted the resignation of the petitioner w.e.f. 14.10.2006.
Having come to know about the order dated 11.6.2007, the petitioner made an application on 2.7.2007 to respondent No.3 (Annexure P/7) for cancellation of the order dated 11.6.2007.

When no action was taken thereon by respondent No.3, on 6.8.2007 the petitioner made an application to respondent No.2/Director,
Public Instructions and later on to the Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:9250 Commissioner,
Directorate of Public Instructions, Raipur on 1.5.2008 vide Annexure P/8.
Vide order dated 31.1.2009 (Annexure P/9), the Director, Public Instructions, Raipur rejected the application of the petitioner for cancellation of the order accepting his resignation.
Aggrieved by the order dated 31.1.2009, the petitioner made an application for review on 20.5.2009 to respondent No.1 which was also rejected vide impugned order dated 22.8.2016 (Annexure P/1).

Hence the petitioner has prayed for following reliefs under para 10 of his petition:
"10.1 That, this Hon'ble court be pleased to issue an appropriate writ in the nature of mandamus setting aside the order dated 22.01.2016 (Annexure P/1) passed by respondent no.1, order dated 31.01.2009 (Annexure P/9) passed by respondent no.2 and the order dated 11.06.2007 (Annexure P/6) passed by respondent no.3.
10.2 That, the respondents are directed to immediate reinstate the petitioner to the post of Head Master, govt. Middle School, Pendri, Janjgir with all consequential benefits including back wages.
10.3 That, the Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to grant any other relief as it may deems fit and appropriate."

03. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the respondent authorities without considering the contents of the application of the petitioner for resignation accepted the same and passed the order whereas the petitioner did not make resignation voluntarily.

The Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:9250 formalities for accepting the resignation as directed by the respondents were not completed by the petitioner and he made an application thereafter to the respondent authorities seeking certain information but even then without passing any order on his application, they passed the impugned order in an illegal and arbitrary manner.

The appellate authority and the revisional Surendra Kumar Upadhyay vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190803494/
2 authority did not consider the grievance of the petitioner properly and rejected his appeal as well as review.

entities.text: Surendra Kumar Upadhyay vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the resignation was tendered by the petitioner only because of threatening being given to him by his wife and as such, it was not voluntarily, the respondent authorities ought not to have accepted the same.
The petitioner has been performing his duties with due honesty and sincerity without there being any complaint or enquiry whatsoever against him.
In these circumstances, the respondent authorities should have considered the applications submitted by the petitioner after tendering resignation and allowed the same.

04. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents vehemently opposing the prayer of the petitioner submits that the petitioner had earlier submitted an application for voluntary retirement on 22.11.2006 to the District Education Officer, Janjgir-Champa and thereafter on 22.12.2006 to District Education Officer, Janjgir-Champa stating that on the date of earlier application i.e.
22.11.2006 he had not completed 20 years of service, therefore, he is again submitting application for voluntary retirement after completion of 20 years of service.
Yet again on 3.1.2007 he submitted an application for Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:9250 accepting his voluntary retirement as his life is in danger.

On 7.4.2007 the petitioner wrote a letter to the District Education Officer stating that he has already submitted one month salary by challan on 19.1.2007 in the office, so his application for voluntary retirement be accepted.
He also made an application on 7.5.2007 stating that till date his resignation has not been accepted by the authority, therefore, the rules for voluntary retirement be provided to him.
Thus, considering several applications made by the petitioner, the District Education Officer vide order dated 11.6.2007 accepted his resignation.

However, against the order dated 11.6.2007, the petitioner filed an application before the Director, Public Instructions, Raipur alleging that his application for resignation has been allowed without completing the formalities.

The Director, Public Instructions, vide order dated 31.1.2009 rejected the application of the petitioner observing that the employer can accept the resignation letter if he is assured that the resignation letter may be accepted.
The review application filed by the petitioner has also rightly been rejected vide order dated 22.8.2016.
Hence there being no substance in this petition, it is liable to be dismissed.

05. In the rejoinder, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner made application for resignation under extreme family pressure but subsequently the same was sought to be withdrawn prior to the order passed by the District Education Officer dated 19.6.2007 which has been admitted by the respondent authorities in their reply.
Even the dues of the petitioner were not settled and in an arbitrary and illegal manner, the resignation was accepted.
As per policy of the State Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:9250 Government, the resignation will not be accepted till the departmental dues are not adjusted.
Copy of the policy of the State Govt is filed as Annexure RJ/1.

He submits that it is settled law that the application for resignation is not maintainable if the same has been given in a forced and involuntarily manner and if the technical formalities pertaining to the resignation have not been followed, the same cannot be accepted.

This apart, vide letter dated 23.6.2007 (Annexure RJ/2) the Block Education Officer directed the petitioner to hand over the charge to one Shivshankar Thawait and through letter dated 30.7.2007 (Annexure RJ/3) the Head Master sought guidance in the matter from Block Educationn Officer which itself reveal that there was jural relationship of employee and employer between the petitioner and the respondents even after acceptance of his resignation and it has not come to an end, therefore, as per CG Civil Services Surendra Kumar Upadhyay vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190803494/
3 Conduct Rules, the petitioner was entitled to withdraw his resignation.

It is an admitted position in this case that the petitioner was appointed as UDT vide order dated 4.4.1987 and he made an application for resignation on 8.12.2006 and again on 3.1.2007.
Respondent No.3 issued a letter on 19.1.2007 to him and directed for completing necessary formalities in this regard and on 11.6.2007 accepted the resignation of the petitioner vide Annexure P/6.
The petitioner again made an application to respondent No.3 for withdrawal of his resignation on 2.7.2007 and thereafter to respondent No.2 on 6.8.2007.

However, on 31.1.2009 (Annexure P/9)
respondent No.2 rejected the application of the petitioner for cancellation of the order accepting his resignation.

Thereafter, the petitioner filed a review application before respondent No.2 which was also dismissed by the impugned order dated 22.8.2016 (Annexure P/1).
08.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner filed application for withdrawal of his resignation letter before settlement of all his retiral dues and as per policy of the State Government, resignation will not be accepted till departmental dues are not adjusted and prior to settlement of departmental dues, it is the fundamental right of the petitioner to seek withdrawal of his resignation.

However, in the present case, the Block Education Officer issued a letter to the petitioner on 23.6.2007 and directed him to hand over the charge to one Shivshankar Thawait which itself shows that the petitioner was still in the department on that date, hence acceptance of letter of resignation of the petitioner is totally contrary to the CG Civil Services Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:9250 Conduct Rules.
09.

Thus, it is clear from condition No.5 of Clause 23 that the accepting authority can determine of his own as to from which date the resignation is to be accepted.
Under Condition No.10, only three circumstances are mentioned in which the resignation can be withdrawn i.e. prior to acceptance of resignation, after acceptance of resignation and after relieving.
In other cases, the resignation can be permitted to be withdrawn only after approval of the government.

10. In the present case, the petitioner submitted his resignation on 3.1.2007 and as per rules, he also deposited one month's salary vide Annexure P/5 and thereafter, vide Annexure P/6 the competent authority accepted the resignation of the petitioner on 11.6.2007 w.e.f. 14.10.2006.

The petitioner did not file any document to show that from January, 2007 to 11th June, 2007, he filed any Surendra Kumar Upadhyay vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190803494/
5 application for withdrawal of his resignation.
11.

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Apex Court in the matter of Shambhu Murari Sinha Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:9250 (supra) observed in paras 16, 17, 18 & 19 of its judgment as under:
"16.

In Power Finance Corporation Ltd. versus Pramod Kumar Bhatia [(1997) 4 SCC 280] this Court went a step further and observed thus:-
"7.

entities.text: Power Finance Corporation Ltd. versus Pramod Kumar Bhatia [(1997) 4 SCC 280]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is now settled legal position that unless the employee is relieved of the duty,
after acceptance of the offer of voluntary retirement or resignation, jural relationship of the employee and the employer does not come to an end."
17. It was pointed out in that case that the acceptance of voluntary retirement was not unconditional and before the conditions could be complied with, the employee could withdraw from the scheme.
On those facts, the above observations were made.
It is not necessary to consider whether in all cases, actual relief becomes the crucial date.

However, the ratio of decision in Balram Gupta case (1998) 9 SCC 559 coupled with the observations of the Constitution Bench in Gopal Chandra Misra case (1978) 2 SCC 301 could usefully be applied to the present case.

18. Coming to the case in hand the letter of acceptance was a conditional one inasmuch as though option of the appellant for the voluntary retirement under the scheme was accepted but it was stated that the "release memo along with detailed particulars would follow".

Before the appellant was actually released from the service, he withdrew his option for voluntary retirement by sending two letters dated 7-8-1997 and 24-9-1997, but there was no response from the respondent.
By office memorandum dated 25-9-1997, the appellant was released from the service and that too from the next day.

It is not disputed that the appellant was paid his salaries etc. till his date of actual release i.e. 26-9-1997, and, therefore, the jural relationship of employee and employer between the appellant and the respondents did not come to an end on the date of acceptance of the voluntary retirement and said relationship continued till 26-9-1997.
The appellant admittedly sent two letters withdrawing his voluntary retirement before his actual date of release from service.

Therefore, in view of the settled position of the law and the terms of the letter of acceptance, the appellant had locus Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:9250 poenitentiae to withdraw his proposal for voluntary retirement before the relationship of employer and employee came to an end.

19. We, therefore, hold that the respondent could not have refused to accept the withdrawal letter of the appellant as it was sent before the jural relationship of employee and employer came to an end.
Consequently, the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside, which we hereby do.
The appellant shall be entitled to rejoin his duty and he shall be paid all his salaries and other benefits during the period he was out from the service.

The learned counsel for the respondent has stated that by this time the appellant might have retired from service on attaining the age of superannuation, if that be so, he shall be paid full salary and allowances for the entire period he was out of service till the date of his retirement and thereafter, he shall be entitled to get all retiral benefits counting the above period as if he was in service."

sentences.text: From the above decision, it is clear that the respondents could not have refused to accept the withdrawal letter of the employee when the employee sent the letter seeking withdrawal of his resignation before the jural relationship of the employee and the employer came to an end.

As per Annexure RJ/2 i.e. letter dated 23.6.2007, the Block Education Officer informed the petitioner to hand over the entire charge of the school to Shri Shivshankar Thawait as his resignation letter has been accepted w.e.f. 14.10.2006.

Further, as per Annexure RJ/3 i.e. a letter dated 30.7.2007 the Head Master intimated the Block Education Officer that despite being directed,
the petitioner has not yet handed over the charge of the school.

Referring to these documents, the petitioner contends that even after acceptance of resignation of the Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:9250 petitioner, he was not relieved from duties and as such, the jural relationship of employee and employer between the petitioner and the respondents having not come to an end, he shall be entitled to rejoin his duties as per aforesaid order of the Hon'ble Supreme Court.

13. The above contention of learned counsel for the petitioner is not acceptable because it is evident from the order dated 11.6.2007 that it is not a conditional order and resignation of the petitioner was accepted from the date of his application i.e. 14.10.2006 and after that, he filed an application for withdrawal of his resignation on 2.7.2007.
Thus, it is clear from this order that jural relationship of employee and employer came to an end much prior to the application seeking withdrawal of his resignation was filed by the petitioner.
Merely because the petitioner did not hand over charge of the school to the incumbent despite being specifically asked for, it cannot be said that such relationship was still in existence.

14. The High Court of Rajasthan in the matter of Narayan Shankar Upadhyay Vs. Rajasthan Rajya Vidhyut Prasaran Nigam Ltd., 2023 SCC OnLine Raj 374, after referring to various judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, held in para 21 of the order as under:
"21.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: By perusal of the above judgments of Hon'ble Apex Court, the position of laws is clear that an employee can withdraw his resignation at any stage before the same becomes effective.

Following the judgment of AIR India Express Ltd. (supra) the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of New Victoria Mills Ltd. V. Shrikant Arya, Civil Appeal Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:9250 No.5655/2021 decided on 27.9.2021 has held that the employee has locus poenitentiae to withdraw the resignation later as the jural relationship between the parties continues till the actual date of his resignation.

entities.text: New Victoria Mills Ltd. V. Shrikant Arya, Civil Appeal Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:9250 No.5655/2021 decided
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The judgments cited by the petitioner are not applicable in the facts and circumstances of this case.

15. In the case in hand, it is not in dispute that the petitioner's resignation was accepted vide order dated 11.6.2007 w.e.f. 14.10.2006 and as per Clause 23(5) of circular of the State Government, the accepting authority on his own can determine the date of acceptance of resignation tendered by the employee.

After passing of this order, the petitioner filed application for withdrawal of his resignation which was duly considered by the competent authority and rejected by well reasoned order dated 31.1.2009 (Annexure P/9) and the review application against the said order was also rejected vide order 22.8.2016 (Annexure P/1).

Therefore, in the totality of facts and circumstances of Surendra Kumar Upadhyay vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190803494/
7 the case, the overall material available on record; the settled legal position and the conditions prescribed for acceptance of resignation; this Court finds no merits in this petition and the same is liable to be dismissed.
16.

Under Condition No.10, only three circumstances are mentioned in which the resignation can be withdrawn i.e. prior to acceptance of resignation, after acceptance of resignation and after relieving.
In other cases, the resignation can be permitted to be withdrawn only after approval of the government.
10. In the present case, the petitioner submitted his resignation on 3.1.2007 and as per rules, he also deposited one month's salary vide Annexure P/5 and thereafter, vide Annexure P/6 the competent authority accepted the resignation of the petitioner on 11.6.2007 w.e.f. 14.10.2006.
The appellant admittedly sent two letters withdrawing his voluntary retirement before his actual date of release from service.
Therefore, in view of the settled position of the law and the terms of the letter of acceptance, the appellant had locus Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:9250 poenitentiae to withdraw his proposal for voluntary retirement before the relationship of employer and employee came to an end.
Thus, it is clear from this order that jural relationship of employee and employer came to an end much prior to the application seeking withdrawal of his resignation was filed by the petitioner.
Merely because the petitioner did not hand over charge of the school to the incumbent despite being specifically asked for, it cannot be said that such relationship was still in existence.
14. The High Court of Rajasthan in the matter of Narayan Shankar Upadhyay Vs. Rajasthan Rajya Vidhyut Prasaran Nigam Ltd., 2023 SCC OnLine Raj 374, after referring to various judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, held in para 21 of the order as under:
"21.
Therefore, in the totality of facts and circumstances of Surendra Kumar Upadhyay vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190803494/
7 the case, the overall material available on record; the settled legal position and the conditions prescribed for acceptance of resignation; this Court finds no merits in this petition and the same is liable to be dismissed.
16.
